highlight.title: What Work Does Generative AI Do?
highlight.summary: Bick, Blandin, Deming and Schumacher build the first task-level genAI adoption indexes from a nationally representative survey linking adoption to detailed occupations and tasks. They find exposure scores explain some but far from all of the variation in adoption, and that adoption is widespread but shallow (NBER WP 35677, Aug 2026).

extractedStats.overlayLabel: NBER: genAI adoption widespread but shallow — fewer than half of workers adopt within most occupations
extractedStats.quote: current adoption is widespread but shallow: genAI is used across many occupations and tasks, yet within most of them, fewer than half of workers adopt

extractedStats.overlayLabel: NBER: exposure scores explain some but far from all variation in actual adoption
extractedStats.quote: Exposure scores explain some, but far from all, of the variation in adoption across occupations and tasks

highlight.title: RPLS US Jobs Report: The US Economy Adds 36.5k Jobs in August
highlight.summary: Revelio's Public Labor Statistics tracker recorded 36,500 net new jobs in August 2026 with active postings falling for a third month. The accompanying AI Labor Market Tracker reports employment in the most AI-exposed occupations down ~6% relative to the least-exposed since before ChatGPT, with the gap reaching 19% among workers aged 22–25, while firm-level evidence shows AI-exposed firms laying off fewer workers than least-exposed firms.

extractedStats.quote: Since before ChatGPT, employment in the most AI-exposed occupations is down around 6% relative to the least-exposed occupations, with the gap reaching 19% among workers aged 22–25
